name: Ji Yujun
current_role: Reportedly head of Xiyingmen Group (textiles), China (unverified)
profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China rich list (~US$150m) with wealth from Xiyingmen Group in textiles. English and Chinese web searches found no public profile confirming the person, the company or their current role.

name: Vijay Sankeshwar
current_role: Founder & Chairman, VRL Logistics / VRL Group (Hubballi, Karnataka)
profile: Born 1950 in Gadag, Karnataka. He started a cargo business in 1976 with one truck and built VRL Logistics into one of India's largest commercial-vehicle fleet owners. He also founded the Kannada newspaper Vijaya Karnataka (sold to the Times Group in 2007) and later Vijaya Vani, and was a BJP MP for Dharwad North. He is chairman, and his son Anand runs VRL as MD.
interesting_fact: His life story, from a single truck to India's largest logistics fleet, became the 2022 multilingual biopic 'Vijayanand'. He received the Padma Shri in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 with one truck bought on a Rs 2 lakh loan and took heavy early losses from accidents and competition. In 1978 the family moved to Hubballi and added three more trucks. His father ran a printing press, B G Sankeshwar & Co., in Gadag.
notes: Both emails appear in VRL's FY2025-26 BRSR filing on NSE. The filing also lists the Company Secretary, Aniruddha Phadnavis (aniruddha@vrllogistics.com), as compliance contact. Better known in Karnataka media and politics. Family-owned Kannada media (Vijaya Vani, Digvijay 24x7) are another route.

name: Githesh Ramamurthy
current_role: Chairman & CEO, CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings (NASDAQ: CCC), Chicago
profile: Engineer turned software executive who joined CCC in 1992, was CTO and President, became CEO in 1999 and Chairman in 2000. He built CCC into a cloud/AI platform connecting auto insurers, automakers and collision repairers. CCC went public via SPAC in 2021, and its insider holdings are the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: He has run CCC as CEO since 1999, more than 25 years, and steered it from claims software into AI, IoT and telematics for the auto-insurance ecosystem. That includes the 2025 acquisition of AI claims firm EvolutionIQ.
deep_cut_fact: Before CCC he was a founding member of Sales Technologies, a field-sales automation pioneer started in 1983 in Georgia Tech's ATDC incubator and later bought by Dun & Bradstreet. He is also credited with designing one of the world's first microprocessor-based cardiac monitors. He studied EE at IIT and CS at Georgia Tech.
notes: Press email is the media contact (Michelle Hellyar, Sr. Director Corporate Marketing) named on CCC's January 2025 EvolutionIQ press release. Check the latest release for current contacts. Data/AI angle fits the podcast.

name: Sultan Ali
current_role: Founder & Chairman, IB Group (Abis Exports India Pvt Ltd), Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh
profile: Co-founded IB Group (Indian Broiler Group) in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh, with his younger brother Bahadur Ali. It grew from a small poultry farm in the mid-1980s into one of India's largest integrated poultry, feed and protein groups. Abis Exports, incorporated in 1998, was the group's backward-integration arm. He chairs the group and oversees its CSR.
interesting_fact: IB Group says it began with a small poultry farm (500 chicks) in 1984, started on the advice of a veterinarian. Some company sources date it to 1985. It became an integrated protein group running contract farming with thousands of rural farmers.
deep_cut_fact: According to his brother's account on the IB Group site, Sultan Ali started the poultry venture in Rajnandgaon with 500 chicks in 1984 after a veterinarian suggested poultry. The company calls 1984-1996 its formative growth period.
notes: Low personal media profile. His brother Bahadur Ali (MD) is the group's public face and does more interviews. The IB Group site was unreachable (503) during research, so no published email was confirmed. Try the group's corporate site or investor-relations page.
